title: Behind The Memo: On Bubble Watch
summary: And the element that keeps markets safe and sane is risk aversion. So that makes people biased toward risk aversion. Those they are risk averse, however, they perform a function, they please the market.

reader_summary.headline: Hello and welcome to Behind the Memo, with Howard Marks.
reader_summary.overview: Hello and welcome to Behind the Memo, with Howard Marks. I'm Harry Whitelaw, and I'm delighted to welcome Howard to explore a recent memo that has received great reader interest. Perhaps because it addresses something that is both enduring and topical.

key_points.text: So Howard, when most of us conceptualize a market bubble, we probably pitch a line on a chart.
key_points.evidence_quote: So Howard, when most of us conceptualize a market bubble, we probably pitch a line on a chart, displaying some kind of financial metric and rocketing upwards.

key_points.text: But you argue that a bubble isn't best defined by numbers, but instead by investor psychology.
key_points.evidence_quote: But you argue that a bubble isn't best defined by numbers, but instead by investor psychology.

key_points.text: The line-rocketing upward on the chart does indicate a bubble, but it doesn't give a sense for a bubble.
key_points.evidence_quote: The line-rocketing upward on the chart does indicate a bubble, but it doesn't give a sense for a bubble.

key_points.text: And I think that you have to have both.
key_points.evidence_quote: And I think that you have to have both.
